note: ALA-LC Bulgarian Romanization Table, 2013 version, p. 1 (letter table) + p. 2 (notes); held source interscript-private-references/alalc/alalc-bulgarian.pdf. Extraction: PDF text layer, every value cell cross-checked against the rendered page image. The map is the 1997 table; the only locally-held printed source is the 2013 version (the table page lists "Earlier versions: 2012, 2011, 1997"). The letter table and notes match what the map encodes, so the rows pin the map against the held printed page; the version difference is recorded here. The value cells for Ц, Ю, Я, Ѣ print the tesh-ligature digraphs (t͡s, i͡u, i͡a, i͡e, U+0361); the text layer stores lookalike Cyrillic glyphs for these — transcribed from the printed image. The upper Ѫ value cell is blank in the text layer and visually identified at 900 dpi as U̐ (U + U+0310), matching the printed lower u̐. Skipped printed rows: Ъ/ъ — the table gives Ъ two value cells: "Ŭ (see note 1)" (the vowel reading, initial/medial) and "ʺ (hard sign)" (the pre-1945 word-final reading). The map implements note 1 with a word-final rule, so a plain-row test of the standalone letter takes the word-final path; both cells are position-dependent per note 1 and not expressible as plain rows. Only the note-1 context is documented here; the Ŭ/ŭ cells were transcribed and failed only because the standalone string is word-final. Canonical-equivalence notes: Й: printed glyph "Ĭ"; the runtime emits the canonically equivalent byte form 'Ĭ'; the row is stored in the runtime's byte form so the byte-exact embedded test passes. | й: printed glyph "ĭ"; the runtime emits the canonically equivalent byte form 'ĭ'; the row is stored in the runtime's byte form so the byte-exact embedded test passes.
